````markdown
# SEC filing ingestion — Roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: your partner's words, 2026-11-06. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md, specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`). uv workspace of four packages: sec-edgar-client, sec-edgar-download, sec-edgar-index-ingest, sec-edgar-ingest.

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | The quarterly and daily index files, ingested into one filing-index table | A | 1 | Small: minutes of downloading at 3 requests/second; about 130 quarterly files since 1993 plus one daily file per business day (SEC full-index and daily-index directories). Measured by Stage 1 |
| O2 | The individual submissions that the index rows name, downloaded | A | 2 | Large: weeks for the full history at 3 requests/second; millions of files (index row count × request rate; not yet measured) |
| O3 | 10-K and 8-K filings handled: picked out of the submissions, with their main documents extracted | A | 3 | Unknown until the submissions are on disk |

Tracks: A — SEC filing ingestion (known progression).

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Filing-index table
      Objective: Build one filing-index table from the real SEC quarterly and daily index files.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: the empty package scaffolds only
      Produces: the filing-index table; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: one table holds the rows of every real quarterly index file from 1993 on and of the daily index files not yet covered by a quarterly file, with each filing appearing once; the findings file records the real run's elapsed time, bytes downloaded and row count
      Leaves out: manifests and traceability (Stage 4); point-in-time awareness (Stage 5); full validation suites (Stage 6); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Submission download
      Objective: Download the submissions that the filing-index table's rows name.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: the Stage 1 filing-index table
      Produces: the submissions on disk, each traceable to its index row
      Exit: over the range the stage spec selects, every index row has its submission on disk or a recorded failure, and the elapsed time and request rate of the real run are recorded
      Leaves out: manifests and traceability (Stage 4); point-in-time awareness (Stage 5); full validation suites (Stage 6); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: 10-K and 8-K handling
      Objective: Pick the 10-K and 8-K filings out of the downloaded submissions and extract their main documents.
      Outcomes: O3
      Consumes: the Stage 2 submissions on disk
      Produces: the 10-K and 8-K main documents, each linked to its filing
      Exit: every 10-K and 8-K among the Stage 2 submissions is listed with its main document extracted to a file, or with a recorded reason it could not be
      Leaves out: manifests and traceability (Stage 4); point-in-time awareness (Stage 5); full validation suites (Stage 6); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: Manifests and traceability
      Objective: Add manifests and traceability across the index, submission and extraction outputs so runs resume and outputs replay from stored bytes.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3 (manifests and traceability)
      Consumes: the outputs of Stages 1–3
      Produces: a manifest recording each source file, its stored bytes and hash, and the outputs derived from it
      Exit: an interrupted run resumes without re-downloading completed files; a re-run from stored bytes with no SEC access reproduces the same table and documents; every output row or document names the source file it came from
      Leaves out: point-in-time awareness (Stage 5); full validation suites (Stage 6); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: Point-in-time awareness
      Objective: Add point-in-time awareness so that later changes to quarterly index files are reconciled without discarding earlier versions.
      Outcomes: O1 (point-in-time awareness)
      Consumes: the Stage 4 manifest and its stored source versions
      Produces: index-table versions that can be read as of a past date, and a record of changes between source versions
      Exit: a re-read quarterly file whose contents changed yields a recorded change set, and the table can be read as it stood before the change
      Leaves out: full validation suites (Stage 6); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Full validation suites
      Objective: Add full validation suites over the index formats, the submissions and the extraction across the supported history.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3 (full validation suites)
      Consumes: the outputs of Stages 1–5
      Produces: committed fixtures and a test suite that runs without SEC access
      Exit: the suite passes in CI on committed fixtures covering each index format in the supported range, malformed sources and the 10-K/8-K extraction cases, and no test downloads from the SEC
      Leaves out: scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 7: Scheduling and deployment
      Objective: Add scheduling and deployment so daily ingestion, quarterly reconciliation and submission download run unattended.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3 (scheduling and deployment)
      Consumes: the outputs of Stages 1–6
      Produces: a deployed, scheduled pipeline with run reports
      Exit: scheduled runs on two consecutive days ingest the new daily index files, with durable run reports showing each run's outcome and any gaps
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note carries this line, which writing-plans copies verbatim into the stage plan's header:

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-ingestion-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

When every stage is ticked, run derive-roadmap §6 over the Outcomes list (O1–O3). Each outcome is met only on path:line or test-name evidence that names the stage plan that built it. A stage stamp alone is not evidence. Each unmet outcome exits as a new stage, which keeps the roadmap live, or as a conscious deferral with a written why.
````

Do you approve this seven-stage partition? Stages 1–3 follow your order, and Stages 4–7 are the hardening stages for manifests and traceability, point-in-time awareness, full validation suites, and scheduling and deployment. On approval I'll commit the roadmap on `main` and hand off Stage 1.
